predecessors.name: Tsardom of Russia
predecessors.text: the Tsardom of Russia in its last Cliopatria year, to which the four Baltic provinces of Nystad were added in September 1721

successors.name: Russian Republic
successors.text: the Russian Provisional Government and Republic, proclaimed 14 September 1917 (RE infobox), after the February Revolution of 8-16 March 1917

ledger.x: 1721, 10 September: Sweden cedes Livonia, Estonia, Ingria and Karelia to Peter I at Nystad.
1721, 2 November: the Russian Empire is proclaimed at Saint Petersburg after the Treaty of Nystad.
1723: Peter I takes the Caspian provinces of Iran.
1727: the court moves to Moscow.
1731, 10 October: the Junior juz of the Kazakhs submits to Russia.
1731, 15 December: the Middle juz swears allegiance.
1732: Russia gives back Gilan, Mazandaran and Astarabad.
1732: the court returns to Saint Petersburg.
1734: about 1,950 Cliopatria cells appear on the Siberian and steppe frontier (lon 27-178 E).
1735: the last Caspian provinces go back to Iran.

1738: 182 of the 200 cells that appear in the Urals and Siberia lie inside the Cliopatria Kazakh Khanate shape of 1737 (about lon 52-61 E, lat 51-53 N, the Orenburg country). kazakh-khanate.json /ledger/32 records the same land as lost to russian-empire in 1738 at confidence 1.
1738: the 18 cells of the 1738 step outside the Kazakh Khanate's 1737 shape (Urals and Siberia, lon 52-96 E, lat 51-77 N).
1739: Russia regains Azov.
1743: Sweden cedes south-western Karelia at Abo.
1752: New Serbia is settled on Zaporozhian land.
1752: the remaining 539 of the 629 cells that appear (about 350 in the Kazakh steppe).
1762: Cliopatria draws East Prussia as Russian.
1762, 5 May: Russia returns East Prussia to Prussia.
1769: Cliopatria's Russian shape takes in steppe land in Ukraine as its Sloboda Ukraine row ends (1768).
1769, 17 September: Russian troops cross the Dniester into Moldavia.
1771, October: Russia abolishes the Kalmyk Khanate and takes its land.
1772, 22 September: the First Partition gives Russia Latgale and eastern Belarus.
1774, 21 July: Kucuk Kaynarca gives Russia the Black Sea shore.
1774, 21 July: the Crimean Khanate is 'formally' independent of both powers but in fact becomes dependent on Russia.
1774, 21 July: the principalities are handed back with the peace.
1775: Cliopatria's Zaporozhian Cossack row ends in 1774 and the Russian shape takes the land in 1775.
1778: about 390 cells appear on the Chukchi coast.
1783: the vassal Khanate is annexed (see the gain).
1783: Russia annexes the Crimean Khanate.
1791: Cliopatria's shape holds Moldavia and Bessarabia for 1791 only.
1792: the principalities are given back at Jassy.
1792: the Ottomans cede Yedisan.
1792: Russian troops invade the Commonwealth.
1793, 23 January: the Grodno Sejm signs the Second Partition.
1793: Russia takes right-bank Ukraine, most of Podolia, eastern Volhynia and Belarus.
1794: Russian forces crush the Kosciuszko Uprising.
1795: Courland and Semigalia pass to Russia.
1795, 24 October: the Third Partition treaty is signed.
1795, 24 October: the Third Partition gives Russia the Vilnius lands.
1796: Cliopatria's shape holds Azerbaijan and Dagestan (45) for this year only.
1797: the cells held in 1796 are gone; bridging from the shape, RP silent.
1799: Russian America.
1801: Russia annexes Eastern Georgia.
1804, 15 January: Tsitsianov storms Ganja.
1804, 15 January: Russia captures Ganja.
1805, 14 May: Karabakh submits to Russia.
1805, 21 May: the Shaki Khanate submits to Russia.
1805, 27 December: Russia accepts the submission of the Shirvan Khanate.
1806: Russian troops take Derbent, Quba and Baku.
1806: Russia occupies Moldavia and Wallachia.
1807: Russia gains Bialystok from Prussia.
1809: Russia gains Tarnopol from Austria.
1809, 17 September: Sweden cedes Finland at Fredrikshamn.
1810: Russia annexes Western Georgia.
1812: Cliopatria drops about 270 cells of Lithuania, Belarus and Poland while the first-french-empire row runs (1812-1813).
1812, 28 May: Russia gives back the principalities except Bessarabia.
1812, 28 May: the Treaty of Bucharest gives Russia Bessarabia.
1813: Russia occupies the Duchy of Warsaw.
1813: the land lost in 1812 is back.
1813, 24 October: the war with Persia ends.
1813: the khanates are absorbed.
1813: the Shaki Khanate is absorbed with the other khanates (RP1: Persia 'recognized Russian possession of all the khanates it held'); the land is part of the gain below.
1813: the Shirvan Khanate is absorbed with the other khanates (RP1: Persia 'recognized Russian possession of all the khanates it held'); the land is part of the gain below.
1813: Gulistan.
1815: the occupation of the Duchy of Warsaw ends as Russia gains Congress Poland.
1815: Russia gains sovereignty over Congress Poland.
1815: Tarnopol goes back to Austria.
1826: the second war with Persia begins.
1827, 24 October: Tabriz surrenders to Paskevich.
1828: the war with Persia ends at Turkmenchay.
1828: Turkmenchay gives Russia Armenia and the rest of northern Azerbaijan.
1828: Cliopatria's shape takes in the Danubian principalities until 1834.
1828, February: the occupation of north-western Iran ends with the war.
1829: Adrianople gives Russia the Black Sea coast of the Caucasus.
1830: Cliopatria removes Congress Poland and lists a 'Poles' row for 1830-1833.
ledger.cpn: Poles (Polish National Government of the November Uprising)

ledger.x: 1834: Congress Poland is back in the shape.
ledger.cpn: Poles (Polish National Government of the November Uprising)

ledger.x: 1834: the principalities leave the shape.
1847: the Junior juz passes under direct rule.
1847: the Middle juz passes under direct rule; the 1822 Regulations had declared Kazakhs 'inorodtsy' (CA).
1847: the Kazakh steppe is Russian.
1848, April: Russia occupies Moldavia after the unsuccessful revolt.
1848, 27 September: a Russian force enters Bucharest.
1851: assumed end of the Moldavian occupation.
1851, April: the Russian and Ottoman occupation of Wallachia ends.
1853, June: Perovsky takes Ak-Mechet on the Syr Darya.
1853, July: Russia occupies the Danubian Principalities.
1854, July: Russia evacuates the principalities.
1856: Russia loses the Danube Delta and Southern Bessarabia after the Crimean War.
1858: the Treaty of Aigun gives Russia the Amur's left bank.
1858: the Ussuri country becomes a Sino-Russian condominium.
1859: Russia takes Dzhulek from Kokand.
1859: the Caucasian Imamate falls.
1860, 14 November: the Convention of Peking ends the condominium.
1860, 14 November: the Convention of Peking gives Russia Primorye.
1861, September: Russia takes Yany-Kurgan.
1862: Russia takes Tokmak.
1864: Circassia falls, the end of the Caucasian War.
1864: Chernayev captures Aulie-Ata.
1864: bridging.
1864: bridging.
1864, June: Veryovkin takes Hazrat-i-Turkestan.
1865, 29 June: Chernayev takes Tashkent.
1866: Russia takes Ura-Tepe and Jizzakh from Bukhara.
1866: Romanovsky takes Khujand.
1867, 18 October: Russia hands Alaska to the United States at Sitka.
1868, May: Samarkand surrenders.
1868, 5 July: Bukhara becomes a Russian vassal.
1870: about 320 Arctic cells (Novaya Zemlya latitudes, lon 52-68 E, lat 71-77 N) appear.
1871: about 106 cells of Xinjiang enter the shape.
1873: Russia takes North Turkmenistan from Khiva.
1873, 4 June: Khiva sues for peace and becomes a protectorate.
1876: Kokand is abolished.
1877: Russia holds the whole of Sakhalin.
1877: Russia gives up the Kuril Islands.
1878, 13 July: Romania cedes Southern Bessarabia.
ledger.cpn: United Principalities of Moldavia and Wallachia (Principality and Kingdom of Romania to 1918)

ledger.x: 1878: Russia takes Kars and Batum from the Ottomans.
1881, May: the Transcaspian Oblast is annexed.
1884, 16 March: Komarov occupies Merv.
1885: the 1871 cells leave the shape.
1885, 30 March (18 March Old Style): Russian troops attack and take Panjdeh.
1895: Russia takes East Tajikistan.
1895: about 119 Arctic cells (lon 136-151 E, lat 73-76 N) enter the shape.
1898, March: Russia leases the Kwantung peninsula.
1900: Cliopatria draws Manchuria as Russian.
1905, 5 September: Portsmouth gives southern Sakhalin to Japan.
1905, 5 September: the Kwantung lease passes to Japan.
1905, 5 September: Russian forces are to leave Manchuria.
1913: about 117 Arctic cells (lon 80-105 E, lat 78-81 N) enter the shape.
1914, 17 August: the Russian army invades East Prussia.
1914: the invasion of East Prussia is defeated at Tannenberg.
1914, April: Tannu Uriankhai becomes a Russian protectorate.
1914, September: Russia wins the Battle of Galicia and begins the siege of Przemysl.
1915: Cliopatria's shape takes in northern Iran.
1915: the Russians are expelled from Poland.
1915: the line is stopped far to the east.
1915, May: the Gorlice-Tarnow Offensive reverses the Russian gains.
1916: Cliopatria's shape takes in eastern Turkey.
1917, March: the empire falls.

wars.name: Great Northern War (closing stage)
wars.outcome: Sweden cedes the four provinces by the Treaty of Nystad, 10 September 1721.

wars.name: Russo-Turkish War (1735-1739)
wars.outcome: Treaty of Nis (3 October 1739): Russia keeps a demilitarised Azov and Zaporozhye and gives up its claims to Crimea and Moldavia.

wars.name: Russo-Swedish War (1741-1743)
wars.outcome: The Treaty of Abo (1743) gives Russia south-western Karelia.

wars.name: Seven Years' War (Russo-Prussian front)
wars.outcome: Treaty of Saint Petersburg, 5 May 1762: Russia returns all lands occupied during the war, East Prussia named.

wars.name: Russo-Turkish War (1768-1774)
wars.outcome: Treaty of Kucuk Kaynarca, 21 July 1774: Russia gains the Dnieper-Bug land, Kerch and Azov; the Crimean Khanate is 'formally' independent and dependent on Russia in fact; the principalities are returned.

wars.name: Bar Confederation and First Partition of Poland
wars.outcome: The partition treaty is ratified on 22 September 1772; Russia receives 93,000 km2.

wars.name: Russo-Turkish War (1787-1792)
wars.outcome: Russia gains Yedisan (1792).

wars.name: Russian invasion of the Commonwealth and Second Partition
wars.outcome: Treaty signed at the Grodno Sejm, 23 January 1793, without Austria.

wars.name: Kosciuszko Uprising
wars.outcome: The uprising is crushed by Russian forces; the Third Partition treaty is signed on 24 October 1795; Russia takes 120,000 km2 with Vilnius.

wars.name: Russo-Persian War (1804-1813)
wars.outcome: Treaty of Gulistan: Persia cedes Georgia, Southern Dagestan and most of Azerbaijan, recognises Russian possession of the khanates.

wars.name: Russo-Turkish War (1806-1812)
wars.outcome: Treaty of Bucharest, 28 May 1812: Russia keeps Bessarabia and returns the other occupied lands.

wars.name: Finnish War
wars.outcome: Treaty of Fredrikshamn, 17 September 1809: Finland becomes an autonomous grand duchy under the emperor.

wars.name: Napoleonic Wars (Russian gains)
wars.outcome: Bialystok from Prussia (1807), Tarnopol from Austria (1809, lost 1815), the Duchy of Warsaw occupied (1813) and given to Russia as Congress Poland (1815).

wars.name: Russo-Persian War (1826-1828)
wars.outcome: Treaty of Turkmenchay (1828): Russia gains Armenia, the rest of northern Azerbaijan and Igdir; Tabriz surrendered on 24 October 1827 and Ardabil was taken on 25 January 1828.

wars.name: Russo-Turkish War (1828-1829)
wars.outcome: Treaty of Adrianople (14 September 1829 on the page, which also gives 2 September): Russia keeps Anapa and Poti, Atskhur, Akhalkalaki and Akhaltsikhe and gains the mouth of the Danube; Ardahan is returned.

wars.name: Caucasian War (1817-1864)
wars.outcome: The Imamate falls in 1859 and Circassia in 1864 (TE).

wars.name: Crimean War (end)
wars.outcome: Russia loses the Danube Delta and Southern Bessarabia.

wars.name: Russian conquest of Central Asia
wars.outcome: Ak-Mechet 1853, Tashkent 1865, Samarkand and the Bukhara treaty 1868, Khiva 1873, Kokand 1876, the Transcaspian Oblast 1881, Merv 1884, Panjdeh 1885.

wars.name: Amur Annexation
wars.outcome: Treaty of Aigun (1858) and Convention of Peking (14 November 1860).

wars.name: Russo-Turkish War (1877-1878)
wars.outcome: Russia gains Kars and Batum oblasts and regains Southern Bessarabia.

wars.name: Russo-Japanese War
wars.outcome: Treaty of Portsmouth, 5 September 1905: Russia cedes its Liaodong leases and southern Sakhalin and evacuates Manchuria.

wars.name: World War I, Eastern Front
wars.outcome: Russia holds most of Galicia from September 1914 to May 1915, is expelled from Poland by mid-1915 and stands on the Riga-Tarnopol line at the end of 1915; ceasefire 15 December 1917.

wars.name: Caucasus campaign (World War I)
wars.outcome: Russian invasion from 1 November 1914; Erzurum falls on 16 February 1916, Trabzon in April 1916, Erzincan on 2 July 1916; the armistice of Erzincan of 5 December 1917 ends the fighting.

wars.name: Persian campaign (World War I)
wars.outcome: Chernozubov enters Tabriz on 30 January 1915; Hamadan falls in December 1915 and Kermanshah in February 1916; the Russian army disintegrates in 1917.

The Chinese frontier by the Aigun and Peking treaties (1858, 1860) and Portsmouth (1905), the western frontier by treaty, the Afghan frontier demarcated 1885-1886 (CA).
